scams.name: Perth Airport Taxi & Uber 'Fake Surge' Overcharge
scams.description: You land at Perth Airport at 6am and try to book an Uber to your hotel in Northbridge. The app quotes $125 — flagged as 3.5× surge — for a trip Google Maps says should be $35. You wait, it creeps higher. You finally switch to a taxi at the rank, which 'agrees' to a flat $90 cash fare. The actual metered fare would be $52.
scams.avoidance: Your fix in 2026 is simpler than ever. Perth Airport's long-awaited rail link opened in late 2022 and connects T3/T4 to Redcliffe and onward to the CBD for under $5 — tourist-proof. Uber and DiDi both have designated pickup bays at all terminals. Wait 10 minutes if the surge is high — surges reset when drivers give up. For cross-check, the standard Uber fare from PER to Perth CBD is $35–$55 off-peak, and the metered taxi is roughly the same plus $5 airport surcharge. Anything over $80 is a scam. Take the Perth Airport train to CBD (<$5, every 15 min) as the tourist-proof option; Use Uber or DiDi from the rideshare bay — typical CBD fare is $35–$55; Compare Uber, DiDi and Bolt before ordering — one is usually normally priced; Wait 10 minutes and retry if surges are extreme — they reset; Insist on meter and card tap for any taxi — screenshot the receipt
scams.location: Perth Airport T1 international, T3/T4 domestic taxi ranks and rideshare bays

scams.name: Perth Facebook / Gumtree Fake Rental Scam
scams.description: You find a Fremantle share-room listed on Facebook Marketplace for $200/week — great photos, a friendly 'landlord' who says he's currently in Melbourne and needs a bank-transfer deposit of $400 to hold the room. You send it. When you arrive in Fremantle, the address is a family home, and the Facebook account has vanished.
scams.avoidance: Your defence is absolute: no in-person viewing, no deposit. For short stays, book only via airbnb.com or booking.com through the official app — never through a Facebook DM or Gumtree listing. For sharehouses, inspect the property and meet current housemates before paying anything. Perth-specific: legitimate listings often cluster on flatmates.com.au and the University of Western Australia's accommodation board; Facebook Marketplace has high fake-to-legit ratios. If scammed, report immediately to National Anti-Scam Centre via ScamWatch and to WA Police via 131 444. Never pay any deposit before an in-person viewing and key handover; Use airbnb.com / booking.com only for short stays, via the app or a bookmarked URL; For sharehouses use flatmates.com.au and inspect in person before paying; Reverse image-search photos in Google Images before any financial commitment; Report scams to ScamWatch at scamwatch.gov.au and WA Police on 131 444
scams.location: Perth CBD, Fremantle, Subiaco, Northbridge — sharehouse + short-stay market

scams.name: Rottnest Island Ferry & 'Day Tour' Upsell
scams.description: You Google 'Rottnest Island day trip' and an aggressive booking site offers 'ferry + bike + lunch' for $139 — 'the cheapest way to visit Rottnest.' You pay. On the day you arrive at Fremantle and learn the ferry portion is with an operator that runs only on odd-numbered weekdays, the bike is a basic unit without helmet, and the 'lunch' is a voucher for a Hotel Rottnest meal that's not actually included.
scams.avoidance: Your defence is to book directly with the two established ferry operators: Rottnest Express (rottnestexpress.com.au, Fremantle and Perth CBD departures) and Sealink Rottnest Island (sealinkrottnest.com.au, Hillarys Boat Harbour and Fremantle). Book the Rottnest Island Authority admission fee separately at rottnestisland.com to avoid bundled markups. Rent bikes on-island at Pedal & Flipper (the official monopoly at the main settlement) or bring your own — in both cases bike rental with helmet is $30 per day. Pay everything by credit card for chargeback protection. Book directly with Rottnest Express (rottnestexpress.com.au) or Sealink (sealinkrottnest.com.au); Buy the Rottnest Island Authority admission separately at rottnestisland.com; Rent bikes on-island at Pedal & Flipper — $30/day with helmet; Pay by credit card for chargeback protection; Read TripAdvisor reviews of the exact ferry operator from the last 6 months
scams.location: Hillarys Boat Harbour, Fremantle B Shed terminal, Perth CBD Barrack Street jetty

scams.name: Fremantle Markets & 'Cappuccino Strip' Overcharge
scams.description: You wander into Fremantle Markets on a Saturday and pick out a pile of touristy pieces — a wooden boomerang, a few didgeridoos, a t-shirt. At the register the total is $245. You paid by tap and didn't check the itemisation. Only later do you notice the 'wooden boomerang' was charged at $89 — an authentic Indigenous-artist piece — when you bought a $25 mass-produced souvenir.
scams.avoidance: Your defence: pay by card and always request an itemised receipt. Don't buy Indigenous art at generic market stalls if the operator can't provide Aboriginal Art Association certification — the Fremantle Arts Centre and the Japingka Gallery are the legitimate sources with artist provenance. On the Cappuccino Strip, menu prices are often posted inside only — ask before ordering if the outdoor seat has a surcharge (it usually does). Use card tap for every purchase so you have receipts to dispute if a total looks wrong. Always request itemised receipts — count the items on the receipt match what you bought; Buy Indigenous art only from certified galleries (Japingka, Fremantle Arts Centre); Check menu prices before sitting outside at Cappuccino Strip cafes; Pay by card tap and screenshot receipts immediately; Challenge rounded totals politely — most operators correct errors when asked
scams.location: Fremantle Markets (South Tce), Cappuccino Strip (South Tce between Collie & High)

scams.name: Perth Backpacker Hostel Prepay Scam
scams.description: You land in Perth on a Working Holiday Visa and a Facebook backpacker group has a 'manager' offering a Northbridge hostel bed at $180/week — pay four weeks upfront by bank transfer and get the first week free. You send $540 (3 weeks). The 'manager' stops responding; the hostel, when you turn up, has never heard of them.
scams.avoidance: Your rule: never pay a hostel before check-in. Verified Perth backpacker hostels (The Old Swan Barracks, Billabong Backpackers, Emperors Crown, Zebra Inn, One World Backpackers) take payment at reception or via HostelWorld/Booking.com — both have platform protection. For sharehouses, insist on in-person viewing and meet current flatmates. Pay rent only after you have keys. The Perth WHV community uses the Perth Working Holiday Facebook group and r/perth itself as crowd-sourced reality check — ask before transferring any deposit. Book hostels only via HostelWorld, Booking.com, or directly at reception; Never pay more than one night's stay before check-in — not even a deposit; Cross-check any Facebook post in the Perth Working Holiday group before paying; Keep a copy of your bank-transfer reference number — needed for WA Police reports; If scammed, file a police report at police.wa.gov.au and ScamWatch
scams.location: Perth CBD and Northbridge hostel market, Facebook/Gumtree WHV groups

scams.name: Northbridge Nightlife Tab Inflation & Card Skim
scams.description: You hand your card to the bartender at a busy Northbridge club to open a tab. At 2am the bill is $380 for a group of four — triple what you actually drank. The card reader 'tapped twice accidentally' on one transaction, there's a $25 'service charge' you weren't told about, and security is visibly close when you review the bill.
scams.avoidance: Your defence is identical to any AU nightlife district. Never open a tab; pay round-by-round with card tap. Keep your card in your wallet and only tap personally. Scrutinise every receipt before signing. If a tab is unavoidable (group purchase), appoint one trusted person to hold it and photograph each drink receipt as it comes back. If overcharged, request the venue manager, photograph the bill, and dispute with your credit card the next business day. Never open a tab — pay round-by-round with card tap; Keep your card in your wallet; tap personally, never hand over; Photograph every bar receipt so totals are verifiable at the end of the night; Challenge bills calmly — request the venue manager and itemisation; Chargeback disputed charges next business day with your bank
scams.location: Northbridge — William Street, James Street, Lake Street nightlife strip
